title: Admin - Content Management - Track Page Update History - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin Content Management - Track Page Update History feature on the Y4J platform. This feature displays page metadata showing the updated date and updated by admin name on each informational page for content accountability. Covers metadata display, accuracy, immutability, and consistency.

testCases.title: Page displays updated date
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content Management page is loaded with at least one page that has been updated.
steps: Navigate to Content Management page
Observe a page entry in the list
Locate the 'Updated date' field
expectedResults: Each page entry displays an updated date
The date is in a recognizable format (e.g., 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'May 25, 2026')
The date is not empty or showing placeholder text
The date represents when the page was last modified
testCases.postconditions: Updated date is confirmed visible on page entries

testCases.title: Page displays updated by admin name
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content Management page is loaded with at least one page.
steps: Navigate to Content Management page
Observe a page entry in the list
Locate the 'Updated by' field
expectedResults: Each page entry displays the name or email of the admin who last updated it
The admin identifier is not empty
The name/email corresponds to a valid admin in the system
The field clearly indicates who made the last change
testCases.postconditions: Updated by admin name is confirmed visible

testCases.title: Updated date changes after editing a page
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A page with a known previous update date exists.
steps: Note the current 'Updated date' of a page
Edit the page (change title or content)
Save the changes
Observe the 'Updated date' after save
expectedResults: The 'Updated date' changes to today's date/time
The previous date is replaced with the current date
The update is reflected immediately in the list
The date is set automatically by the system
testCases.postconditions: Updated date reflects the latest edit

testCases.title: Updated by admin name changes after editing a page
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin (pv@mailto.plus). A page exists that was previously updated by a different admin.
steps: Find a page that was last updated by a different admin (or 'System')
Edit the page and save changes
Observe the 'Updated by' field
expectedResults: The 'Updated by' field now shows the current admin's name/email (e.g., 'pv@mailto.plus')
The previous admin name is replaced
The field is updated automatically by the system
It reflects who made the most recent change
testCases.postconditions: Updated by reflects the current admin

testCases.title: Metadata persists after page refresh
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Pages with update metadata are displayed.
steps: Note the 'Updated date' and 'Updated by' for a specific page
Refresh the browser page (F5)
Find the same page in the list
Compare the metadata
expectedResults: After refresh, the 'Updated date' is unchanged
After refresh, the 'Updated by' is unchanged
Data is loaded from the backend (persisted correctly)
No data loss occurs on refresh

testCases.title: Metadata is read-only (cannot be edited by admin)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Pages with metadata are displayed.
steps: Observe the 'Updated date' and 'Updated by' fields on a page entry
Attempt to click on or interact with these fields
Open the edit modal and check if these fields are editable
expectedResults: The 'Updated date' is read-only (not clickable, not editable)
The 'Updated by' is read-only (not clickable, not editable)
No edit controls exist for these metadata fields
The edit modal does NOT allow changing update history
These fields are system-managed only
testCases.postconditions: Metadata is confirmed immutable via UI

testCases.title: Date format is consistent across all pages
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Multiple pages are displayed.
steps: Navigate to Content Management page
Observe the 'Updated date' on multiple page entries
Compare the date formats
expectedResults: All pages use the same date format
No inconsistencies in formatting across entries
Dates are unambiguous and readable

testCases.title: Newly created page shows creation metadata
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. About to create a new page.
steps: Create a new informational page
After creation, find the new page in the list
Observe the 'Updated date' and 'Updated by' fields
expectedResults: The new page shows today's date as the updated date
The 'Updated by' shows the current admin who created it
Metadata is set automatically upon creation
No manual entry is required
testCases.postconditions: New page has correct initial metadata

testCases.title: Metadata is visible on paginated pages
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page list has multiple pages (pagination).
steps: Navigate to Content Management page
Verify metadata on page 1 entries
Navigate to page 2 (if pagination exists)
Verify metadata on page 2 entries
expectedResults: Update metadata is displayed on all pages of the list
Each entry shows its own correct metadata
Pagination does not hide or break the metadata display

testCases.title: Metadata does not change when page status changes (Draft to Published)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A draft page with known metadata exists.
steps: Note the 'Updated date' and 'Updated by' for a draft page
Publish the page (change status from Draft to Published)
Observe the metadata after status change
expectedResults: If publishing counts as an update: metadata updates to current date/admin
If publishing is a separate action: metadata may or may not change (depends on implementation)
Either way, the metadata is consistent and accurate
No data corruption occurs
testCases.postconditions: Metadata is consistent after status change
